name: idle-vivarium-boulders-day-a
refs: IMAGE 1, THE AUTHORITY (room 1's signed painting by day): the device, the camera, the lens, the scale, the finish and the light. Never the layout of its planting:

IMAGE 2, THE LAYOUT MAP (structure and placement only, never the look): green-grey is the back zone where the tall planting stands; the red line is the floor's back edge (the amber strip above it is the only allowed slack); pale sand is the open floor; dark brown at the foot is the soil strip; dark grey columns are the device walls with the feed line, mister and vent; the white frame is the part that must hold the room's main feature; the hatched corner must not hold it:
IMAGE 3, SUBJECT AND MATERIAL ONLY (sandstone stone and scree): never its flat, toon-like finish, never its angular flat-topped slabs:
prompt: Output a NEW image, 16:9. The SAME terrarium inside the SAME rugged field device as Image 1, seen from the same eye height with the same lens and the same depth of field: the left wall with its braided feed line and connector, the right wall with its mister arm and slatted vent, the dark soil strip along the foot, each exactly where it is in Image 1. Inside it a NEW planting, painted in the Miniature Lives finish of Image 1: fine grain on the world, soft bokeh behind, a warm key light from the top left with its shafts. Cute by craft, never childish: no cartoon outlines, no toy colours, no gloss, no glow, no chrome, no alien tech. No creatures, no animals, no figures, no text, no letters, no digits, no logos, no frame, no UI. No water except one small flat seep. Pebbles and leaves at the scale of Image 1's. THE NEW PLANTING: two great rounded sandstone boulders, smooth and weathered, with lichen and moss in their cracks. The large one fills the back left (from about 12 to 41 percent of the width, its top at about 35 percent of the height); the smaller one stands right of centre (from about 55 to 70 percent of the width, its top at about half the height). Both are domed and rounded all over: no flat top, no ledge, no cliff, no climbable face, no crag. Fans of fine scree at their feet stop at the floor's back edge. Cushion plants and small succulents in the gaps. The floor: fine scree, small pebbles, moss and low cushion plants, two rounded stones at most. The stone is warm ochre-grey sandstone lit from the top left, its shadow side warm, never blue granite. Do NOT copy Image 1's burrow, root mound, succulents or its pool: Image 1 is the authority on the device, camera, scale, finish and light only. THE OPEN FLOOR (the pale band of Image 2, from the red line down to the dark soil strip) is low open ground, nothing a small creature could perch on: every piece on it lower than a pebble-and-a-half (about 32 px of a 568 px tall picture), at most two rounded or leafy pieces up to about twice that, never flat-topped; no flat raised top, no ledge, no slab, no step; no log, root or stem lying across the floor; everything tall stands BEHIND the red line, its feet ending on it, never spilling forward onto the floor. The back edge of the floor (where open floor ends and the planting behind begins) runs along the red line of Image 2, or a little above it inside the amber strip, never below it. The two dark side columns of Image 2 hold only the device walls, the feed line at the left and the mister and vent at the right, kept clear of planting.
